transcript:
[doctor] Hello, Mr. Matthews. Good to see you again. How have you been feeling since your last visit?

[patient] Hi, Doctor. Not great, to be honest. My lower back pain has been pretty bad, and now it’s radiating down to my right leg.

[doctor] Hmm, that's concerning. Can you tell me more about the pain and when it started?

[patient] Sure. The pain started about 8 weeks ago. At first, it was on and off, but now it's happening every day. It gets worse when I walk or stand for a long time.

[doctor] I see. On a scale of 1 to 10, with 10 being the worst pain you've ever felt, how would you rate your pain?

[patient] It’s around a 7 or 8 most of the time.

[doctor] And does the pain interfere with your sleep or daily activities?

[patient] Yes, it does. I can’t sleep well, and it’s hard for me to do my job as a warehouse worker. I also used to enjoy cycling, but I can’t do that anymore.

[doctor] I understand. Have you tried any medications or treatments to relieve the pain?

[patient] I’ve taken some over-the-counter pain meds, but they don’t really help much.

[doctor] Have you experienced any tingling or numbness in your right foot?

[patient] Yes, I feel tingling and numbness in my right foot quite often.

[doctor] Any muscle weakness in your right leg?

[patient] Yes, my right leg feels weaker than usual.

[doctor] Alright. Have you had any difficulty walking or standing?

[patient] Yes, walking and standing are really tough for me now.

[doctor] Have you noticed any other unusual symptoms?

[patient] No, just the pain, tingling, and numbness.

[doctor] Let's go over your past medical history. You have hypertension and type 2 diabetes, correct?

[patient] Yes, that’s right.

[doctor] Are you taking any medications for those conditions?

[patient] Yes, I take medication for both my blood pressure and diabetes.

[doctor] Alright. Let’s proceed with a physical examination. I’ll start by checking your vitals. Your blood pressure today is 135/85 mmHg, and your fasting blood glucose level is 110 mg/dL.

[patient] Okay, sounds normal?

[doctor] Yes, they are within the acceptable range. Now, let’s check your neurological function. I’ll perform a straight leg raise test on your right leg. Please let me know if you feel any pain.

[patient] Ouch, yes, that hurts.

[doctor] That’s a positive straight leg raise on the right. I’ll also test your sensation in the L4-L5 dermatome. Do you feel this?

[patient] It feels a bit reduced compared to my left side.

[doctor] I see. There’s also some muscle weakness in your right lower extremity.

[patient] What does all this mean?

[doctor] Based on your symptoms and the physical exam findings, it looks like you might have lumbar radiculopathy, which means there's likely nerve root compression in your lower back.

[patient] Oh, I see. What do we do next?

[doctor] We’re awaiting the results of an MRI of your lumbar spine to confirm the diagnosis. In the meantime, I’ll prescribe Pregabalin 75 mg to help manage the neuropathic pain.

[patient] How often should I take it?

[doctor] You’ll take it twice daily for 30 days. I’ll also administer a corticosteroid injection to reduce inflammation and pain.

[patient] Okay, that sounds good. What else can I do to help with the pain?

[doctor] I’ll refer you to physical therapy. They’ll provide you with exercises to strengthen your back and improve mobility.

[patient] How long will it take for the pain to get better?

[doctor] It varies from person to person, but we’ll evaluate your progress in 4 weeks when you come back for a follow-up visit.

[patient] Alright, I’ll do that.

[doctor] Additionally, we need to discuss some lifestyle modifications. A balanced diet with more vegetables and fewer processed foods can help manage your conditions.

[patient] I’ll try to eat healthier.

[doctor] It's also important to quit smoking and reduce alcohol consumption if you do those things.

[patient] I’ll work on that too.

[doctor] Great. I’ll provide you with some educational materials on managing hypertension and diabetes. It’s crucial to keep those under control to prevent exacerbation of your symptoms.

[patient] I understand. I’ll read those materials.

[doctor] Regular monitoring of your blood pressure and blood glucose levels is also important. Do you have any questions or concerns about the treatment plan?

[patient] No, I think I understand everything. What if the MRI results are not good?

[doctor] Depending on the MRI results, we might discuss further interventions, including the possibility of surgery if conservative measures don’t work.

[patient] I hope it doesn’t come to that.

[doctor] We’ll do our best to manage this conservatively first. Also, I know there are financial constraints and insurance restrictions, but it’s important to follow through with the MRI.

[patient] I’ll make sure to get it done.

[doctor] Excellent. You’ll also need to monitor your symptoms and let us know if anything changes or worsens.

[patient] I will.

[doctor] Do you have any other questions or concerns?

[patient] No, I think that’s everything.

[doctor] Alright, Mr. Matthews. I’ll see you in 4 weeks for a follow-up. Take care and stay in touch if you need anything.

[patient] Thank you, Doctor. I appreciate it.

[doctor] You're welcome. Take care and see you soon.
